sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 67. Whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living separately, whether under a decree of separation or otherwise, without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

sections.heading: Explanations
sections.body: Explanation.—In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 63

learningObjectives: Understand the offence of sexual intercourse during marital separation under BNS s. 67.
Analyze the requirement: absence of wife's consent during separation under decree or custom.
Examine the statutory penalty: imprisonment from two to seven years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 67 provides that whoever has sexual intercourse with his own wife, who is living separately from him, whether under a decree of separation or otherwise, without her consent, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: While general marital rape remains subject to Exception 2 of s. 63, the law strictly revokes marital immunity once the spouses are living separately under a court decree or custom. Non-consensual sexual intercourse during separation constitutes a distinct penal offence.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 67 (corresponding to IPC s. 376B).
Condition 1: Living separately (under a decree of judicial separation or otherwise under custom/agreement).
Penalty: Imprisonment not less than two years, extending to seven years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The parties are legally husband and wife.
The wife is living separately from the husband.
The separation is under a decree of separation or otherwise.
The husband engaged in sexual intercourse with her without her consent.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 67 recognizes that when a marriage has broken down to the point where the wife is living separately—whether under a formal decree of judicial separation passed by a family court, or through de facto separate living under custom or mutual agreement—the husband has no marital claim over her body. If he forces sexual intercourse upon her without her consent, he cannot invoke Exception 2 of s. 63. He is punished under s. 67 with imprisonment of two to seven years.
examples: Teaching example (Judicial separation decree): A family court grants a decree of judicial separation to a wife. The husband visits her independent apartment at night and forces sexual intercourse upon her against her will. Section 67 applies; the husband faces up to seven years imprisonment.

Teaching example (De facto separation): A wife leaves the matrimonial home due to cruelty and resides in her parents' home for two years. The husband corners her and forces intercourse without consent. Section 67 ('or otherwise') directly covers de facto separation.
distinctions: Section 67 vs Section 63: Section 67 specifically penalizes non-consensual intercourse by a husband during separation (2 to 7 years); general rape under s. 63 carries 10 years to life.
Living together vs Living separately: The marital exemption only operates while the wife is cohabiting with the husband; separation activates s. 67.
problemApplication: Issue: What is the liability of a husband who forced sexual intercourse on his wife who was living in a separate rented flat pending divorce proceedings?
Rule: Under BNS s. 67, sexual intercourse by a husband upon his wife living separately without her consent is an offence punishable with two to seven years imprisonment.
Application: The parties were living separately, and intercourse occurred without the wife's consent.
Conclusion: The husband is liable under s. 67.
